n1.speaker: leslie
n1.text: George is wearing his poppy today. It's Remembrance Sunday. Do you know about it?

translations.fa: جورج امروز گل شقایقش را زده. یکشنبهٔ یادبوده. دربارهٔ اون می‌دونی؟

branches.suggestion: Not really. Why do people wear poppies?
branches.suggestionFa: نه واقعاً. چرا مردم گل شقایق می‌زنن؟

branches.suggestion: I've seen poppies everywhere this week.
branches.suggestionFa: این هفته همه‌جا گل شقایق دیدم.

n2.speaker: leslie
n2.text: To remember people who died in wars. Poppies grew on the battlefields after the First World War.

translations.fa: برای یاد کسانی که تو جنگ‌ها مُردن. بعد از جنگ جهانی اول گل‌های شقایق تو میدان‌های جنگ رویید.

branches.suggestion: George, did your family fight in the war?

cultureNote.en: Remembrance Day is on 11 November. At 11 a.m. people keep a two-minute silence.
cultureNote.fa: ۱۱ نوامبر ساعت ۱۱ دو دقیقه سکوت می‌کنند.

branches.suggestion: He must have been very brave.
Did he tell you stories about it?
branches.suggestionFa: براتون قصه دربارهٔ اون تعریف می‌کرد؟

n4.speaker: leslie
n4.text: He never talked about it, did he, George? A lot of men from that generation didn't. But he would always go to the service every year.

translations.fa: هیچ‌وقت دربارهٔ اون حرف نمی‌زد، نه جورج؟ خیلی از مردهای اون نسل حرف نمی‌زدن. ولی همیشه هر سال به مراسم می‌رفت.

branches.suggestion: I understand. Some memories are too painful.
Do you still go to the service?
I'd be honoured to come with you.
Yes, of course. Thank you for asking me.
branches.suggestionFa: آره، حتماً. ممنون که ازم خواستید.

n6.speaker: leslie
n6.text: That means a lot to him. We'll leave at half ten. Wrap up warm — it's always cold at the memorial.

translations.fa: این براش خیلی ارزش داره. ساعت ده و نیم راه میفتیم. لباس گرم بپوش — کنار یادبود همیشه سرده.
